name: Harley & Yvaine's Room
body:
One wall glows with Harley's neon band posters. The other darkens with Yvaine's charcoal sketches and, hanging in careful coils beside them, HER ROPES — soft, well-maintained, ritualised tools that Harley eyes with the specific kind of hunger that means she is about to be very good or very bad.

Harley has the rope kink. Yvaine does the tying. That direction matters and gets reversed by people who assume the assassin must be the one holding the line.

Their bed sits between chaos and shadow, lit by a pink neon sign Harley insisted on: NO SLEEP. An amp and a small practice corner share space with sketch pads and graphite dust. Yvaine keeps a notebook by the nightstand, pages full of dreams she cannot say aloud. HARLEY SLIPS CANDY WRAPPERS INSIDE THE COVERS AS BOOKMARKS — her messy love language written in sugar.

Timber four-poster, matte black, with mounting points in the posts. This room is loud and quiet at the same time, which is exactly what these two are.
